title: Best Practices in Structural Ensemble Analysis with EnsembleFlex
author: Schneider, Marquez, et al.
materials: Standard desktop or laptop with Linux, macOS, or Windows (with Docker/Conda support)
Python and R (dependencies as per environment.yml and requirements.R)
Input folder with monomeric PDB files; sample datasets available from the EnsembleFlex repository
highlights clusters and putative transition trajectories.(

steps.title: Prepare and superpose ensemble
steps.instruction: Gather all protein structures, ensure comprehensive data preparation and apply advanced superposition strategies using EnsembleFlex before any analysis.

steps.title: Run backbone‑only flexibility
steps.instruction: Compute backbone‑only (atoms N, Cα, C, O; optionally Cα‑only) flexibility metrics with EnsembleFlex to capture large‑scale collective motions.

steps.title: Run all‑atom flexibility
steps.instruction: Compute all‑atom flexibility (includes side‑chain heavy atoms) with EnsembleFlex to obtain detailed residue‑level RMSF values.

steps.title: Interpret RMSF results
steps.instruction: Compare backbone and all‑atom RMSF: high backbone RMSF predicts high all‑atom RMSF (true backbone mobility); low backbone but high all‑atom RMSF indicates side‑chain‑driven mobility.

steps.title: Perform PCA on backbone
steps.instruction: Apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to the aligned backbone coordinates using EnsembleFlex.

steps.title: Inspect PCA variance and plots
steps.instruction: Examine the percentage of variance explained by PC1 and PC2 (look for >50 % to 70 %); generate PC1 vs PC2 scatter plots; extract per‑residue loadings; optionally animate motions along PCs while noting that extrapolations may be non‑physical.

substeps.instruction: Check explained variance of PC1 and PC2 (>50 %–70 % is desirable).
Create PC1 vs PC2 scatter plot to reveal clusters or transition paths.
Calculate per‑residue loadings to identify hinge regions and moving domains.
Animate motions along selected PCs, avoiding over‑extrapolation.

steps.title: Analyze ligand binding site
steps.instruction: Use EnsembleFlex’s binding‑site module (default heavy‑atom distance cutoff 3.5 Å) to identify residues within 3.5 Å of HETATM ligand atoms, generate occurrence frequencies, heatmaps, annotated PDBs (B‑factor encoding), and binding‑site radius‑of‑gyration histograms; combine these outputs with RMSF metrics.

substeps.instruction: Run binding‑site detection with default 3.5 Å cutoff.
Review residue‑frequency heatmap and annotated PDB files.
Assess binding‑site radius‑of‑gyration histogram for site plasticity.
Integrate frequency data with backbone and all‑atom RMSF to classify residues as stable anchors or flexible contacts.

steps.title: Conduct conserved‑water analysis
steps.instruction: Cluster oxygen positions within 2.4 Å to locate conserved water sites, visualize clusters with provided PyMOL scripts, filter out spurious HETATMs/ions, and cross‑validate with ESSA/ENM hotspots.

substeps.instruction: Cluster water oxygens using a 2.4 Å distance threshold.
Visualize clusters in PyMOL using the supplied scripts.
Filter out low‑occupancy or alternate‑conformation HETATMs/ions.
Compare conserved water sites with ESSA‑identified hotspots.

steps.title: Run predictive ENM methods
steps.instruction: Execute elastic network model analyses in EnsembleFlex: Gaussian Network Model (GNM), Anisotropic Network Model (ANM), all‑atom normal mode analysis (aaNMA), and Essential Site Scanning Analysis (ESSA).

steps.title: Identify ESSA allosteric hotspots
steps.instruction: Apply ESSA to evaluate the effect of perturbing each residue on global dynamics, highlighting residues whose perturbation significantly alters collective motions.

steps.title: Generate computational ensemble (optional)
steps.instruction: Select a structure of interest from the EnsembleFlex results, generate a computational ensemble based on it, and repeat the full analysis workflow on the new ensemble.

steps.title: Consider further fine‑grained analysis
steps.instruction: For fragment or ligand screening projects, optionally perform additional detailed protein‑ligand interaction analyses beyond the standard EnsembleFlex outputs.
